exclusives.description: 2002 landlord restrictive covenants: while ≥15,000 SF is operated as a supermarket, no other food supermarket / food-for-off-premises in the center (carve-outs: snack bars, ice cream, candy, package liquor, ≤2,500 SF food in variety/dept stores, ≤600 SF pet food, sit-down restaurants). cite.doc: Amendment of Lease and Expansion Agreement

goDark.value: Permitted. Tenant may cease operations at any time in its sole discretion on 60 days' notice; the Landlord's SOLE remedy is to collect rent as and when due — Landlord waives any right to accelerate rent, collect damages, or seek injunctive relief. Recapture lever: if a ≥15,000 SF supermarket goes dark, Fixed Annual Additional Rent increases by $0.50/SF of the Demised Premises while no supermarket is open; after the 4th anniversary of cessation, that increase applies only to the area then still vacant.

cite.doc: Amendment of Lease and Expansion Agreement

assignment.value: Tenant may sell, mortgage, assign, sublet, or license all or part of its interest WITHOUT Landlord consent, one or more times, to anyone (including Related Entities), for any lawful use — but neither Tenant nor Royal Ahold (guarantor) is released; any assignee must assume in writing. A 'New Lease' recapture-protection mechanism lets the Original Tenant require a fresh lease if an assignee defaults/rejects in bankruptcy.

cite.doc: Amendment of Lease and Expansion Agreement

camTax.value: Taxes: Tenant pays Proportionate Share of real estate taxes (Land share originally 27.40%), with a Tenant right to contest added in 2002. CAM: Proportionate Share (originally 27.90%) + 15% administrative overhead; capital expenditures excluded (repaving ≥20% of the blacktop in 12 months is deemed capital); annual reconciliation; Tenant audit right (once per Lease Year — if Landlord overstates by >3%, Landlord pays the audit cost up to $2,500 + interest). Tenant may even assume CAM maintenance via self-help if dissatisfied.

defaultTerms.value: Monetary default: 20 days after written notice, plus a 'Second Notice' and a further 10 days, before Landlord may terminate. The Ahold guaranty gives the Guarantor an additional 15 days to cure after notice.

flags.issue: Renewal-period date calendar shifted between documents
flags.detail: The 2002 Amendment's Exhibit K uses an April-1 calendar (e.g., 1st renewal ~4/1/2025), while the 2023 extension letter sets the current period at 5/1/2024–4/30/2029. The 2023 letter is the latest controlling document, so the 5/1 calendar governs the current period; later option windows here are projected at 5-year increments off that date.

flags.issue: Options are evergreen / tenant-cancellable, not affirmative-exercise
flags.detail: The eleven 5-year Extension Periods auto-renew unless Tenant gives ≥12 months' notice to terminate (§2.03(a)). Economically the tenant controls a ~55-year tail; the landlord cannot force a roll.

narrative: Super Stop & Shop (tenant of record The Stop & Shop Supermarket Company) anchors the Concordia Shopping Center in Monroe Township, NJ under a 6/30/1983 Indenture of Lease originally signed by Mayfair Super Markets, which merged into Stop & Shop in 2000. A 2002 Amendment of Lease and Expansion Agreement expanded the premises to a built 65,572 SF, reset a new 20-year term, and wholesale-replaced the go-dark, assignment, options, and default provisions; Royal Ahold (Koninklijke Ahold) guarantees all financial obligations. The lease is strongly tenant-favorable: eleven evergreen 5-year extension periods (the first running 5/1/2024–4/30/2029 at $750,603/yr), a right to go dark with the landlord's only remedy being to keep collecting rent (plus a modest $0.50/SF bump), and a no-consent assignment right. Landlord interest sits under a 1997 master net lease held by Concordia Holding. Key reconciliation note: the renewal-rent dollars come from Exhibit K of the 2002 Amendment, and the current-period dates are governed by the later 2023 extension letter.
